changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: For finance-led buyers (CFO or controller owning month-end close), open with: Know where your money is, deposit by deposit, at month-end. Every deposit matched to its transactions and invoices, so close takes days, not a week of matching by hand. Then go straight to M9 and offer a walkthrough on one month of their own statements. Keep checkout and APIs as supporting detail, even when the inbound mentions an ordering portal.
changes.why: The standard deck opened on our global-infrastructure framing and drew no reaction until payout reconciliation came up, and the buyer talked about 'the deposits' and wanting 'to know where my money is', never 'payments' or 'infrastructure'.

changes.current_line: Proven ROI, backed by an independent economic impact study.
changes.change: For finance buyers, replace the study claim with an offer: Send us one month of your statements and we'll show you what manual deposit matching and unmatched deposits cost you, in your hours and your write-offs. Build the figure from the customer's own statements and people costs, and record the model and final number so the next rep can reuse it.
changes.why: The rep put the deal at 20 percent ('Dead, honestly'), and it closed after Wen built a cost figure from the customer's statements, which the CFO accepted because 'that's my number, not yours'.

changes.current_line: Trusted by leading businesses; see our customer stories.
changes.change: For distributor and wholesale buyers, do not offer retail or software case studies as proof. Offer a peer reference call with a wholesale or distributor customer that runs invoice-based reconciliation on us. If none exists yet, flag it to customer marketing as a gap to fill before the next deal of this kind.
changes.why: The CFO asked twice for a distributor peer, dismissed the retail substitute with 'this is a company that sells sweaters', and never got the call.

changes.current_line: Support plans with tiered response times, up to 24/7 coverage.
changes.change: Against bank-channel incumbents, frame support as a named person who owns your account and knows your setup, not as tiered response times. Pair it with reconciliation visibility, and do not lead on rates.
changes.why: The incumbent's only known move was a rates offer the CFO rejected ('I didn't ask about my rates'), and the one new question she asked afterwards was whether she'd get a named contact.
